angle: Movement translation, DL (clearest of five groups screened, Fig 2B): each lineman's tracked Combine 40 start laid over his own random NFL pass-rush starts (combine_frames vs game_frames_sample, first 1.5 s from first movement, alignment-adjusted). Five per-player drill-to-game similarity scores tested for pressure beyond pick on held-out classes (null); the NFL-side first step is the usable signal, and a frozen Both list (NFL first step + official 40) is compared honestly with same-size draft-order, 40-only and first-step-only lists.
metric_name: First step: speed 0.3-0.5 s after first movement on ~20 random sampled NFL pass rushes, alignment-adjusted, in sd after weight and EDGE share; translation = five similarity scores between that and the same window/curve of his tracked Combine 40
headline_number: Drill-to-NFL translation after size rho 0.07 [-0.17, 0.31], n=67; no similarity score moves pressure more than 0.3 pts per sd beyond pick (all 95% intervals span zero, n=52). NFL first step: 0.8 pts per sd [-0.1, 1.6] held out (shuffle p 0.01), 0.7 [0.0, 1.5] with window chosen inside each fold; rank rho with pressure-over-forecast 0.27 [0.00, 0.50] (n=69), 0.34 [0.01, 0.62] day-3/UDFA (n=36); rank-correlation gain over pick forecast 0.05 [-0.08, 0.16]. Same-size lists on raw pressure: first step alone 9.8%, Both 10.0%, earliest picks 10.3% (Both minus pick -0.3 [-2.2, 2.0]) at median pick 66/78 vs 18.
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of round_16/cand_3 (8.19, best score on the translation angle), applying round-25 judges' top_changes by analogy. (1) Plain scout-language title and lede that answer the angle's question directly (no). (2) All intervals unified at 95%. (3) Table 1 rebuilt as the translation test: all five drill-to-game similarity scores through the same held-out slope test, plus each side alone. (4) Nested selection: the first-step window chosen inside each leave-one-class-out training fold with the no-tracking forecast refit inside the fold. (5) Ranking quality with player-bootstrap CIs: held-out Spearman (all 69 and the 36 day-3/UDFA men), rank-correlation gain over the pick forecast, Brier gain of the rule. (6) Softened claims: four same-size lists on raw pressure show Both ties draft order (-0.3 pts) and the 40 half adds nothing over the first step alone; the stated value is draft price, not better projection. (7) Viz: Fig 2 cut from three panels to two (held-out slopes moved to Table 1), Fig 4B replaced (it duplicated Table 2) by same-size list comparison, matched-pair figure cut to one panel, figure numbering follows text order, 2026 table slimmed. (8) Johnson/Jean-Baptiste illustration and veteran-price paragraph dropped. Pre-registration hash unchanged (e3079960bd2d). check.py: 1,889 words, 5 figures, 3 tables.
open_risks: At 95% the headline NFL first-step slope interval touches zero ([-0.1, 1.6]); only the shuffle p (0.01) and the nested estimate's lower bound (0.0) keep it from reading as a null
Both rule (frozen in round 16) is shown here to add nothing over the NFL first step alone (9 of 10 vs 8 of 10); judges may ask why the frozen rule keeps the 40 half
Raw-pressure tie with draft order means the value claim rests on draft price (median pick 66-78 vs 18), not on finding better rushers
Translation null is partly a measurement ceiling (single-rep 40 first-step repeatability 0.54, ceiling 0.67)
Window z-scores standardized over all three classes (weight/role residual only), a small leak in the nested check
Small lists: ten rushers, three on day 3; matched-pair sign test p 0.17
